risks.note: Named as a key industry risk factor in the Chairman's message: global VCM credit prices and retirement volumes remain subject to significant cyclical and structural volatility driven by macroeconomic conditions, buyer sentiment and integrity-related market events, with the 2023-2025 contraction seeing retirement volumes decline even as per-tonne spending rose. risks.note: Flagged as the most acute near-term policy risk: the United States' withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and rollback of federal climate regulation depress global carbon market sentiment, and participants everywhere are exposed to regulatory reversals affecting demand for voluntary credits. EKI's stated hedge is its growing focus on India's domestic CCTS compliance market, driven by domestic legislation independent of US policy, plus adjacent credit markets.
risks.risk: Regulatory and policy reversal risk in international markets

risks.note: Corporate buyers face increasing scrutiny from regulators, civil society and the media over the integrity of their climate claims. Although the litigation and reputational exposure sits primarily with buyers, it creates indirect demand-side pressure on the VCM and has driven the 'greenhushing' phenomenon in which buyers purchase but do not publicise; 40% of high-durability CDR offtake transactions in 2025 did not disclose the buyer.
risks.risk: Greenwashing litigation and reputational risk carried by credit buyers

risks.note: Management states directly that the VCM downturn, buyer hesitation from geopolitical uncertainty, budget compression from inflation and the anti-ESG agenda 'have materially impacted market liquidity and our near-term revenues' - an acknowledged, already-realised hit rather than a hypothetical, which prompted the FY 2024-25 strategic reset of consolidating non-core subsidiaries, rationalising costs and preserving liquidity.
risks.risk: Near-term revenue pressure from the VCM downturn and the anti-ESG environment

currentContext.expansion: EKI's expansion in FY26 was structural and portfolio-led rather than plant-led - it is an asset-light climate-services business with no manufacturing capacity of its own. The principal corporate action is the demerger of the Generation Segment into wholly owned subsidiary EKI One Community Projects Limited, filed under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013 in the previous financial year, with the Board's Report stating that during the year under review the necessary approvals and regulatory processes progressed in line with the proposed scheme; completing the demerger is a named strategic priority for FY 2026-27. On the group-structure side, EKI acquired additional equity shares in GHG Reduction Technologies Private Limited, taking its shareholding to 100% and making it a wholly owned subsidiary, to strengthen control and improve operational, administrative and governance alignment. GHG Reduction Technologies deliberately avoids owning capacity, running a Just-in-Time model under which cookstoves, Surya Nutan units and water filters are manufactured under an outsourcing model against confirmed orders or sourced externally. Project-pipeline expansion runs through subsidiary Amrut Nature Solutions: Project TRIBAL, a community agroforestry / SALM project across the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh, was registered under the Verified Carbon Standard during the year; Project TASAR, an ARR project in Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand, completed Gold Standard validation; and Amrut completed its assigned technical scope on Project Aranya, a large-scale carbon project in Central India, delivering the CCB Project Description and supporting documentation. Forward expansion intent is to build a robust NbS project pipeline across India and Southeast Asia using Amrut's capabilities, to scale ESSPL's advisory capacity for BRSR Core / CBAM / CCTS compliance work, and to enter India's domestic Carbon Credit Certificate market, which the Chairman's message describes as set to commence trading by mid-2026 on regulated power exchanges under the CERC Regulations, 2026 and as a new revenue stream structurally protected by regulatory mandate.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Named as a key industry risk factor in the Chairman's message: global VCM credit prices and retirement volumes remain subject to significant cyclical and structural volatility driven by macroeconomic conditions, buyer sentiment and integrity-related market events, with the 2023-2025 contraction seeing retirement volumes decline even as per-tonne spending rose. Management's stated mitigant is the pivot to high-integrity, CCP-labelled and Gold Standard certified typologies plus fee-based advisory revenue through ESSPL, so the model is 'no longer dependent on VCM volume alone'.
- Flagged as the most acute near-term policy risk: the United States' withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and rollback of federal climate regulation depress global carbon market sentiment, and participants everywhere are exposed to regulatory reversals affecting demand for voluntary credits. EKI's stated hedge is its growing focus on India's domestic CCTS compliance market, driven by domestic legislation independent of US policy, plus adjacent credit markets.
- Corporate buyers face increasing scrutiny from regulators, civil society and the media over the integrity of their climate claims. Although the litigation and reputational exposure sits primarily with buyers, it creates indirect demand-side pressure on the VCM and has driven the 'greenhushing' phenomenon in which buyers purchase but do not publicise; 40% of high-durability CDR offtake transactions in 2025 did not disclose the buyer.
- Management states directly that the VCM downturn, buyer hesitation from geopolitical uncertainty, budget compression from inflation and the anti-ESG agenda 'have materially impacted market liquidity and our near-term revenues' - an acknowledged, already-realised hit rather than a hypothetical, which prompted the FY 2024-25 strategic reset of consolidating non-core subsidiaries, rationalising costs and preserving liquidity.
- The auditor's Emphasis of Matter records that the Board approved the scheme of arrangement demerging EKI into EKI One Community Projects Limited effective January 1, 2025 or such other date as the NCLT may fix, that NCLT approval is still awaited, and that the standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026 have accordingly been prepared without giving effect to the scheme. Completion of the demerger is also a named FY 2026-27 strategic priority, so the corporate structure and reported financials remain contingent on a pending tribunal outcome.
- Demand in the VCM is increasingly concentrated among fewer, larger buyers who now routinely conduct third-party audits, demand site-level transparency and insist on documented biodiversity and community co-benefits before committing. Management explicitly cites diversification across compliance and voluntary segments, geographies and project typologies as the means of reducing this concentration risk.
- The CCC market is set to commence trading by mid-2026 on regulated power exchanges under the CERC Regulations, 2026, but the specific floor and forbearance price values - which will set the effective lower and upper bounds of the market - had not been formally notified by BEE and CERC as of the date of the report, leaving the economics of EKI's most-emphasised new revenue stream unsettled.
- GHG Reduction Technologies Private Limited, now a wholly owned subsidiary, continued to operate in a challenging business environment due to persistent volatility in the carbon market, and manages that exposure by running a Just-in-Time model under which cookstoves, Surya Nutan units and water filters are outsourced or sourced externally only against confirmed orders.
